chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
That he used to glorify with the glorification of Fatima (peace be upon her), so he would connect it and not break it.

key_terms.تَسْبِيحَ: Glorification (specifically referring to the Tasbih of Fatima)

ai.seo_question: What is the practice of reciting the Tasbih of Fatima after prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Imam’s consistent practice of reciting the Tasbih of Fatima (peace be upon her) immediately after prayer, emphasizing the importance of maintaining a continuous, uninterrupted flow of dhikr. In Shia tradition, this act is not merely a ritual but a profound spiritual discipline that connects the believer to the Ahl al-Bayt, reinforcing the link between prophetic prayer and the intercessory merit of the Imams. The continuity (wasl) signifies a state of spiritual presence and devotion that extends the sanctity of the prayer into daily life.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Muhammad Bin Ja’far, from the one who mentioned it,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws that heasws used to Glorify by the Glorification (Tasbīḥ) of Syeda Fatimaasws, so heasws would recite it without interruption’.
en.sarwar: 12. It is narrated from the narrator of previous Hadith from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ya‘qub ibn Yazid from Muhammad ibn Ja‘far from those whom he has mentioned has said the following:
“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would say Tasbih of Fatimah al-Zahra’, ‘Alayha al-Salam, continuously without interruption.”
